para.bold: How to calculate halite (solid phase) enthalpy at the triple point ?

listitem.para: The enthalpy of molten NaCl (liquid phase) $ H_l $ can be calculated from Eq. 21 of Driesner2007Part2 by subsituting $ X_{NaCl} = 1 $.
The enthalpy difference $ \Delta H_{fus} = H_l - H_h $ of phase changing (solid phase to liquid phase) can be calculated from Eq. 28 of Driesner2007Part2.
(1). Clapeyron slope of the NaCl melting curve is $ \frac{dP}{dT} = \frac{1}{a} = 4044325.810887325~ Pa/K $; (notice the unit!)

(3). Volume of melting at triple point $ \Delta V_{fus} = \frac{1}{\rho_l} - \frac{1}{\rho_h} = \frac{1}{1561.224722497394} - \frac{1}{1912.0183915214473} = 0.00011751525885297855 ~ kg/m^3 = 6.867944273144626\times 10^{-6} ~ m^3/mol$ (see Rho_Liquid and Rho_Solid, and M).

Therefore, $ \Delta H_{fus} = \frac{dP}{dT}\times T_{Triple}\times \Delta V_{fus} = 4044325.810887325 \times 1073.85 \times 6.867944273144626\times 10^{-6} = 29827.476978550334 kJ/mol $ which is constent with value $ 29.8 ~ kJ/mol $ in Driesner2007Part2.
Enthalpy of halite at triple point temperature $ H_h(T_{Triple}, P) = H_l(T_{Triple}, P) - \Delta H_{fus}(T_{Triple}, P) $.

xrefdescription.para: Confirm that $ \Delta H_{fus} (T_{melting}, P) = H_l(T_{melting}, P) - H_s(T_{melting}, P) $ ?

detaileddescription.para:
The constant $ C(P) $ in the above equation
We easily calculate the constant C(P) once get $ H_h $, so $ C(P) = H_h(T_{Triple}, P) - H_{halite}(T_{Triple}, P) $.

simplesect.para: Just like the description in 2.2.4 of Driesner2007Part2 : "Pure NaCl vapor as a separate phase exists only at pressures substantially lower than those encountered in any geological system", no worries that the (T, P) point occurs in pure vapor region of NaCl (See figure at Boiling_p(const double& T)), i.e. NaCl always present as liquid or solid state in the geological T-P conditions.
